full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J.: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.5.92 passed by the Division Bench of the High Court Division, Dhaka, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 869 of 1991 and Criminal appeal No. 1246 of 1991 concerning the release of one Nilima Biswas alias Musammat Salma Begum, daughter of appellant Atul Chandra Biswas which arose in pursuance of the Special Tribunal Case No. 188 of 1991. 

 2. The short fact relevant for disposal of this appeal is, Nilima Biswas alias Musammat  Salma Begum was allegedly Kidnapped on 19.5.91 by accused Salahuddin. Thereafter, the First Information Report was lodged by the father of the girl and the Special Tribunal Case was started against the added respondent Salahuddin under Section 4(C) of the Cruelty to Women's (Deterrent Punishment) Act, 1983. The case of the girl was that she was a major girl aged about 19 years at the time of marriage with Salahuddin on the basis of a registered Kabinnama. 

 3. The Tribunal case is pending for disposal. In the meanwhile the question of custody of the girl came up for consideration in an appeal before the High Court Division in Criminal Appeal No. 3246 of 1991 which arose from the order of the Tribunal releasing the girl. The father of the girl also filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case being Case No. 869 of 1991 demanding the custody of the girl as she is a minor girl. 

 4. It appears that the learned Judges of the High Court Division, while disposing of the criminal appeal also disposed of the miscellaneous case filed by the father of the girl out of turn and without hearing the Advocate of the appellant. 

 5. Leave was granted to consider whether the learned Judges of the High court Division were correct in disposing of Miscellaneous Case No. 869 of 1991 under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure when there was an earlier order for disposal of both the cases together. The miscellaneous case was listed for hearing before the Division Bench as Item No. 76 and the matter was taken up out of turn without any notice to the learned Advocate for the appellant. 

 6. In view of the leave granted by us, it is patently unwarranted in law to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case relating to the custody of the allegedly minor girl while disposing of the appeal out of turn without giving any opportunity to the other side. The Court not only disposed of the appeal by the impugned order but also directed that the appellant Nilima Biswas @ Salma Begum should be released from custody and allowed to go wherever she liked. This order, in fact, amounts to disposal of the Miscellaneous Case on merit without hearing the parties. 

 7. Dr. Ahmed Husain learned Advocate appearing for the added accused-respondent, finds it difficult to support the judgment of the high Court Division as the Miscellaneous Case was disposed of out of turn without entering into the merit of the case. 

 8. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 869 of 1991 is remanded to the High Court Division for disposal on merit in accordance with law.
